newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Philippines reveals treasury benchmarks for Brady.
newsitem.headline: Philippines reveals treasury benchmarks for Brady.

text.p: The Philippines set the U.S. Treasury benchmark rate to be used in determining the price and yields of the 2017 and 2018 bond exchanges following its invitation on September 2 to exchange one set of Brady bonds for another, arranger J.P. Morgan said on Wednesday.
The U.S. Treasury benchmark rate is 7.0 percent, which gives the 2017 bond exchange a yield of 8.30 percent on a price of US$823.43 per US$1,000 of principal.
The 2018 exchange bond yield is also 8.30 percent on a price of US$827.18 per US$1,000 principal amount.
The minimum fixed rate bond exchange yield is 9.25 percent.

The Philippines has offered to exchange the series B principal collateralised interest reduction bonds due 2017 and the series A principal collateralised interest reduction bonds due 2018 with new fixed-rate bonds due 2016 and floating rate bonds due 2011.
The invitation to make the exchange expires on September 20 with a settlement date of October 7.
